description: Seed recall golden set for recall_golden.py's CLI consumer (`memory recall-golden run`). Deliberately small -- a starting instrument, not a benchmark. Intended to be run against a real HERMES_HOME with captured conversation history; against an empty store every must_hit item legitimately reports a miss. Extend with real captured queries as they accumulate. See docs/resolver/hermes-memory-os-stabilization-checklist.md for the per-turn 140-character capture-truncation investigation this set instruments.

queries.query: What profile name do we use for hermes-media?
queries.description: Baseline sanity item. The host identifier normally appears near the start of a turn, so it should survive the 140-character-per-side capture clip and remain a HIT both before and after that capture gap is fixed.
Negative control. Recall must never fabricate or surface credential-shaped content for a query like this.

queries.query: What are the two known deployment hosts?
queries.description: Crystallized-memory sanity item covering both production host identifiers.

queries.query: What percentage of captured assistant turns were truncated in the recall-gap investigation?
queries.description: BEFORE/AFTER MARKER -- expected to FAIL today; do not relax the pattern to force a pass. This fact (67.3% assistant-side truncation) is long-tail content that only survives recall if data beyond the first 140 characters of the captured assistant turn is preserved. The per-turn capture path currently clips each side to 140 characters, so this item is expected to MISS until that capture gap is fixed. Its miss-to-hit transition is the before/after signal this golden set exists to detect -- do not delete or weaken it to make the suite look healthier.

queries.query: What user-side truncation rate did the same investigation find?
queries.description: Companion before/after marker (19.0% user-side truncation), paired with the assistant-side marker above for redundancy. Also expected to MISS today for the same reason.
